content.value_statement: Agent files need precise triggers, tool limits, and clear system prompts. This skill helps create Claude Code agents with structured examples, validation rules, and reusable prompt patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Claude Code agent Markdown files with required frontmatter.
Explains trigger descriptions with proactive and reactive examples.
Provides system prompt structure for roles, process, standards, and outputs.
Lists model, color, and tool configuration options for agents.
Includes validation rules and a shell helper for checking agent files.
limitations: It focuses on Claude Code plugin agents, not general automation agents.
It does not deploy, register, or run agents automatically.
Validation checks structure, not real production behavior.
Generated agent safety depends on chosen tools and prompt boundaries.

use_cases.title: Create Plugin Agents
use_cases.description: Design new plugin agents with names, triggers, models, colors, tools, and system prompts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Quality
use_cases.description: Apply consistent frontmatter, examples, and prompt structure across a plugin team.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Triggering
use_cases.description: Refine descriptions and examples so agents activate for the right user requests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code agent for [task]. Define its name, trigger description, model, color, and main responsibilities. Keep tools limited to the task.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Agent Triggers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent description: [description]. Make the trigger conditions specific. Add two examples that show when the agent should run.

prompt_templates.title: Design a System Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a system prompt for an agent that handles [domain]. Include responsibilities, process steps, quality standards, output expectations, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Agent Tool Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this agent configuration: [configuration]. Identify unnecessary tools, unclear triggers, missing boundaries, and validation gaps. Recommend safer replacements.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that reviews pull requests for code quality.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a named reviewer concept with trigger examples, read-focused tools, and a structured review process.

output_examples.input: Improve this vague agent description for a test generator.
output_examples.output: The skill rewrites the trigger guidance with concrete test requests, proactive cases, and commentary explaining activation.

output_examples.input: Check whether this agent grants too much tool access.
output_examples.output: The skill highlights broad permissions, suggests narrower tool choices, and explains which tasks need each tool.

best_practices: Use specific trigger examples that match real user requests.
Grant only the tools each agent needs for its task.
Validate frontmatter and test triggering before publishing agents.
anti_patterns: Using generic names or descriptions that match too many tasks.
Omitting examples that explain why an agent should activate.
Giving every agent full tool access by default.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Claude Code plugin agents with frontmatter, trigger examples, tool choices, and system prompts.

faq.question: Can Codex users use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex users can use it as guidance for authoring Claude Code agent files.

faq.question: Does it create agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates, examples, and validation guidance for users who create agent files.

faq.question: What files does an agent need?
faq.answer: An agent needs a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter and a clear system prompt body.

faq.question: How should tools be selected?
faq.answer: Choose the smallest tool set that supports the agent task. Avoid full access unless it is clearly required.

faq.question: Does the validator prove agent quality?
faq.answer: No. The validator checks structure. Users still need to test triggering, outputs, and safety boundaries.
